title: Introspection and the debug adapter
preamble:
# Introspection and the debug adapter

The integrator-facing debugging surface, in two halves. First, the read-only
introspection APIs an inspector calls on a running engine: working-memory
queries, schema / rule metadata, DS-source mapping, Rete-network topology,
match tracing, refraction, and truth-maintenance justifiers. Second, the **DAP**
wire protocol the DS debug adapter (`ds dap`) exposes them through —
session lifecycle, execution control, breakpoints, variable inspection, the
custom `ds/*` requests, and the reverse-execution contract. An integrator
building its own inspector calls the engine APIs directly; one running the DS
adapter gets the same surface over DAP without writing C.

## What this is not

- Not the rule-author debugging guide — see
  [LDEB], which states
  the language-level observability commitments. This doc states how they are
  delivered.

Debugging is an **integration** concern: a subprocess and a wire format are
not things DS itself has.
